# file: # THE SINGLE DECLARATION OF EVERY LEDGER TABLE'S SHAPE.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#   gates.tsv grew a 4th column (expires_after). Three things knew the width and
#   only one of them was updated:
#     1. bin/feedback.sh   -- taught the new width
#     2. bin/ledger.sh     -- asserted NF!=3, rejected every committed gates row
#     3. bin/verify.sh     -- its fixtures wrote 3-field gates rows, so fixing
#                             (2) broke the positive control in check 8
#     4. this file's own header comment named 3 columns above 4 of data
#   Four sites, one class, and the third was created by the fix to the second.
#   A width that is written down in four places is a width that will disagree
#   with itself. It is written down once now, here, and read by:
#     bin/schema.sh   validates every table against this file
#     bin/ledger.sh   delegates its shape assertion to schema.sh
#     bin/verify.sh   builds its fixtures at the declared width
#   The header line of every table is CHECKED against this file, not trusted.
#   A comment that describes data is data, and drifts like data.
# SELF-REFERENCE: this file has a row for itself. A schema that does not
# describe itself is the one table nobody validates.
# COMPLEMENT: schema.sh also fails if a .tsv exists in ledger/ with no row here.
# The registry cannot quietly omit a table, because the directory listing is the
# enumeration and the disagreement is what is reported.
SCHEMA.tsv
classes.tsv
sites.tsv
gates.tsv
friction.tsv
events.tsv
translations.tsv
absences.tsv
